newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania rulers and Socialists talk for first time.
newsitem.headline: Albania rulers and Socialists talk for first time.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democratic Party and the nation's biggest opposition party, the Socialists, on Friday held head-to-head talks for the first time since last May's disputed general election.

President Sali Berisha's right-wing Democrats invited the Socialists, heirs to the former communists, to discuss nationwide unrest over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes but the parties failed to find common ground.

The Socialists boycotted parliament last year after alleging that the Democrats intimidated voters and stuffed ballot boxes in the election, which was also criticised by foreign observers as failing to meet international standards.

"I made clear our party position, namely the resignation of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government and the formation of a technocrat government which would rule the country until early elections," senior Socialist Pandeli Majko told reporters.

Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu, who is also foreign minister, said the fact the Socialists were prepared to open up a dialogue was a positive move but he said the protests were not a political issue.
"It's not about politics. People protest because they lost their savings and our party has concrete solutions to minimise such big losses," Shehu told reporters, without elaborating.

The United States and Europe urged Albania's political parties to begin a dialogue to seek to halt two months of unrest. But the opposition has demanded early elections as an answer to the disorder but Berisha has rejected the demand.
"Dialogue is a nonsense as long as the opposition is politically persecuted and students and pupils are being beaten by police," Majko said.
